messages:
sanjay: Hey team — bringing up a new cluster in ap-south1 (mum-1) for a private tenant. Need a focused perf validation and kernel/driver sanity run before handoff. Can @maya and @jonah take lead on throughput/latency baselining? tagging @tania for networking/MTU checks. infra-bot: pls schedule a smoke window.

maya: On it. I'll run the kernel/driver checks first. Quick checklist I'm planning:
- verify nvidia driver + cuda toolchain
- check MIG/NVLINK topology where applicable
- run short perf jobs for p50/p95 baseline (short seq)
- validate prefix cache hit behavior

jonah: I'll do sustained throughput runs after maya's sanity pass. Want to measure tokens/s, tail latency under continuous batching, and dropout behavior when we hit buffer limits.

kai: Heads up — some of the ap-south1 images default to mtu=1500; for our RPC fanout we prefer 9000. @tania can you confirm if the subnet supports jumbo frames or if I should request infra net config change? :eyes:

tania: I checked with cloud-net team — regional subnets currently support 9000 but some older NIC firmware in the cluster nodes may still negotiate 1500. I'll coordinate a rolling firmware check. For the runbook, we should include an `ethtool` check: 
```
ethtool -k eth0
ethtool -S eth0 | head -n 30
```
Also add `ip link show` to check MTU.

maya: Doing driver checks now. Steps and outputs I'm logging: 
1) driver presence
```
$ modinfo nvidia | head -n 5
filename:       /lib/modules/5.15.0-xx/nvidia.ko
version:        535.54
```
2) gpu visible and ECC status via `nvidia-smi -q`
3) cuda toolkit quick smoke: `nvcc --version` and run `deviceQuery` sample.

infra-bot: scheduled perf-smoke window at 2026-03-18T10:00Z (30m). Channels: #eng-infra.

jonah: Quick note on kernel params — we saw on staging that `vm.max_map_count` and `ulimit -n` affect our multi-worker throughput. Add checks: 
```
$ sysctl vm.max_map_count
vm.max_map_count = 262144
$ ulimit -n
65536
```
If low, we should set via init scripts.

sanjay: Good call. Include those in runbook. Also ensure `tcp_retries2` and `tcp_fin_timeout` are defaulted for cloud. Lowering can help for short-lived RPC spikes.

maya: Kernel module validation done. Observed one node with `nvidia` failing soft init (driver mismatch). Took node out of rotation, reinstalled driver 535.54, rebooted, passed. Logging note: if re-install, ensure `dkms` hooks are present or AMI will drift.

jonah: Starting a baseline throughput job — short synthetic load to estimate tokens/s for typical gen workload. Using our bench harness: 
```
bench/runner --model llama2-7b --seq 1024 --batch 4 --duration 300 --measure latency,throughput
```
Initial results (node type A100S 80GB equiv): p50 42ms, p95 120ms, throughput ~950 tokens/s per GPU with batching=4. Recording in shared spreadsheet.

tania: Network checks: found 2 nodes with MTU stuck at 1500 because of old NIC driver. I pushed a remediation plan: upgrade igb_uio driver and force re-provision network. ETA 45m. Will mark those nodes as maintenance.

kai: Also saw NVLINK topology inconsistent on one rack; `nvidia-smi topo -m` showed missing links between GPUs 2 & 3 on node-12. Could be cabling or firmware. We'll run `nvswitch` diag and open hardware ticket if needed.

maya: After fixes, re-ran bench. New numbers: p50 38ms, p95 95ms, throughput ~1030 tokens/s. Looks consistent across 8 nodes. Noted that enabling intra-node batching bump gave diminishing returns beyond batch=8.

jonah: Important regression check: compare to baseline in eu-west cluster. Tokens/s ~5% lower in ap-south1 due to slightly older GPU microcode and lower network fabric perf. Recommendation: either accept 5% perf delta in cost model or request newer SKU images. Add note to handoff doc.

sanjay: Can we produce a short runbook snippet for handoff? Suggested sections: 
- cluster summary (node types, driver versions, kernel)
- pre-handoff checklist (driver, kernel params, MTU, nvlink)
- perf baseline table (p50/p95/tokens/s) with command to reproduce
- known issues and mitigations

maya: Here's the reproduce snippet to include: 
```
# kernel and driver
modinfo nvidia | grep version
nvidia-smi -q | grep -E "Driver Version|CUDA Version|ECC Mode"
# perf
bench/runner --model llama2-7b --seq 1024 --batch 4 --duration 300 --output csv > baseline.csv
# network
ip link show dev eth0 | grep mtu
ethtool -k eth0
```

tania: I'll add the MTU remediation steps and commands to detect firmware NICs.

kai: Cost note for handoff — these nodes currently billed on spot; for guaranteed performance SLA we should recommend reserved capacity for tenant X. Add cost delta estimate: ~+28% for reserved vs spot but reduces preemptions that hurt p95.

jonah: Also added a quick check for caching behavior: run 3 sequential short requests to see KV cache warm-up time. If cold-start penalty > 15ms, call out for cache tuning.

infra-bot: performed node-health check: 95% nodes healthy, 2 nodes in maintenance (driver, mtu).

sanjay: Great work. @maya @jonah can you assemble final handoff doc and paste into /runbooks/mum-1-handoff.md? Include the reproduce commands and the perf CSV. I'll review and schedule handoff to platform team. :thumbsup:

maya: Will do, uploading in 30m.

jonah: I'll attach the raw bench CSV and a short summary with recommendations on reserved vs spot for the tenant workload.

sanjay: Closing loop — once docs are in, we'll run a single end-to-end smoke with a canary tenant and signoff. Thanks all! :party_popper:
